better_modelling: Keep the axe as E22 and the deposit as A2 Stratigraphic Volume Unit. The existing flat find->context link is AP21 contains (A2 -> E18) and is not false, only silent: expand it to its declared full path, an A7 Embedding with AP18 is embedding of -> the axe and AP19 is embedding in -> the A2 deposit, which is what Martin Doerr, Martijn van Leusen and Achille Felicetti settled in t1123. Then carry the two dates separately so residuality is inferable rather than asserted by a new term (Minimality): the axe's E12 Production P4 has time-span -> Neolithic, and the deposit's A4 Stratigraphic Genesis (A5, related via AP13 has stratigraphic relation to) P4 has time-span -> post-Roman. Optionally record the recovery as S19 Encounter Event with O19 encountered object -> the axe, whose scope note is where the in-situ question ('supports the assumption that the object was not moved since the archaeologically relevant deposition event') actually lives. No 'residual find' class is needed and none exists.
reasoning: A applies AP18 (A7 -> E18) and AP19 (A7 -> A2) inside their declared domains and ranges, its A7 and S19 scope-note quotations are verbatim, and its three t1123 quotations and their attributions to van Leusen, Doerr and Felicetti all verify; it is suboptimal only because it never names AP21 contains, the declared shortcut its own path expands, and never says concretely where the Neolithic date goes (E12 Production, P4 has time-span), which is the excavators' actual question. B is wrong on two counts: it endorses the fully developed path through E9 Move for a natural colluvial relocation, and E9 is a subclass of E7 Activity, whose scope note restricts it to 'actions intentionally carried out by instances of E39 Actor' - Doerr's t0674 gloss ('by man or nature, such as meteorites'), which B quotes accurately, is about P53's scope note, not about E9's actor requirement, so it does not license the move it is used to license. B then rejects the CRMarchaeo route on the false premise that no class for a stratigraphic context is available here, when A2, A7, AP18, AP19 and AP21 all resolve in this corpus and the SIG answered this precise question ('finds are described as objects embedded in Stratigraphic Units (A7 Embedding)'), and its final advice - keep the flat link unchanged - forgoes the one construct whose scope note already carries the intrusion caveat this case turns on. B's E93/P195/P167/P164 alternative is itself domain- and range-clean, which is why this is a clear rather than total margin.
